**Work context**

Fabian is a secondary school student currently living in the Botoșani area of Romania, studying subjects including Romanian language, mathematics, and computer science (informatică). He is preparing to relocate to Northampton, England to live with his father, with September enrollment at a school there — Silverstone UTC (his preferred choice given its engineering focus at the Silverstone F1 circuit) or Weston Favell Academy as a confirmed backup.

**Personal context**

Fabian has a strong hands-on engineering and tech identity spanning sim racing, 3D printing (Bambu A1 with AMS Lite, plus a resin printer), electronics/Arduino projects, PC building, home networking, and video editing. He runs an informal creative brand called "Chartreuse" (with sub-teams CRT — Chartreuse Racing Team, CTIT, and CDT — Chartreuse Design Team) and makes cinematic car edits for Instagram using BeamNG.drive footage. He has a collection of analog watches and appreciates understated, quality aesthetics across hardware and media. His music taste for edits leans toward underground, atmospheric, and melancholic electronic music (e.g., Burial) rather than mainstream phonk.

**Top of mind**

Fabian recently explored OSINT tools and personal privacy/address exposure, particularly Romanian-specific resources and command-line tools like Holehe and Sherlock. He is also working through Romanian school geometry (right triangle altitude and projection formulas), having requested step-by-step explanations in Romanian with intuitive analogies rather than formal proofs.

**Brief history**

*Recent months*

Fabian has been heavily active across several interconnected projects. His **sim rig build** is a major ongoing effort: he owns an FFBeast wheelbase, plans a custom GT flat-bottom steering wheel (laser-cut aluminium, suede wrap, ~80–120€), and is designing a 40×80 aluminium extrusion frame with a secondhand bucket seat; his XG438QR 43" 4K monitor (needing a 19.5V replacement power brick) is earmarked as the dedicated rig screen, with his LG 34" OLED ultrawide staying as the main desk monitor. He has a DIY FFB wheel project in his garage workshop that was broken at time of discussion. G923 pedals are his current setup with a load cell mod as an interim upgrade and Heusinkveld Sprint as the aspirational endgame. Budget is approximately £1,510.

His **BeamNG cinematic content** work has been active and detailed: he has produced edits including an Escalade/S-Class convoy to a Succession soundtrack and an S-Class edit, and was planning a European luxury convoy edit on a New York-style map (MBWR City). He uses Zeit graphics mod, Medal for capture, and has received a copyright strike on Instagram for using "In and Out of Love." He understands royalty-free music needs and prefers underground atmospheric tracks.

On the **hardware/electronics** side: he repaired an MKS ODrive Mini v1.0 motor controller (shorted ABZ/Hall connector pins), worked on an ODrive S1 with hoverboard motors, purchased a Pinecil V2 soldering iron kit, and identified a PT1000 temperature sensor from salvaged heating wiring for potential Arduino reuse. He troubleshot his Bambu A1 after an AMS Lite drop incident. He built a full home NAS on a 2008 AMD Phenom machine running TrueNAS SCALE with RAIDZ1, Syncthing, Tailscale, Minecraft Forge server, and Homarr.

He runs a **Discord server** for sim racing/gaming (ACC, LMU, ETS2, BeamNG, CS2) with friends and was configuring Carl-bot reaction roles and channel structure. He investigated BeamMP security after a breach. His home network uses Digi fiber in Romania with an ASUS router, WiFi 6/6E card, and a dual-network Windows setup routing Air Link over Ethernet and general traffic over WiFi via interface metric configuration.

He has been doing **school support** across Romanian grammar (possessive pronouns, indefinite pronouns), geometry, math (systems of equations, repeating decimals), and a communism report. He is also a beginner Python learner (PyCharm, list comprehensions, modules, pendulum library, NumPy/matrices).

*Earlier context*

Fabian explored Fusion 360 simulation types for a center-of-gravity school experiment using aluminium and Static Stress analysis. He set up Firefox with privacy extensions after switching from Opera, added Romanian school-year calendar events to Google Calendar, and researched Silverstone UTC admissions ahead of an April England trip. He asked about DCS World vs. Arma 3 for helicopter simulation, and researched DJ controllers (Pioneer DDJ FLX4) for his sister. He troubleshot ReShade for a night vision effect in BeamNG and worked through a BeamNG cinematic project involving helicopter scripting with Bell 407 mods and multi-vehicle recording workflows.

*Long-term background*

Fabian has long-standing interests in automotive aesthetics and sim racing (ACC, LMU, BeamNG), with content creation as a consistent creative outlet. His engineering identity — building, repairing, and tinkering across software and hardware — is a foundational trait. He got into watch collecting through his father and has a taste that skews toward quality and understatement. He is comfortable with casual, direct communication and mild language, prefers concise practical help over formal explanations, and actively self-corrects when misunderstood.

project_memories.019d269c-9f21-7633-8030-3f537ef49282:
**Purpose & context**

Fabian is a student in Romania building a DIY e-ink tablet from scratch to replace textbooks and a pen for school use. The project has two competition targets: ONCS (roughly 2 months out) and RoSEF (later), which drives a phased strategy — functional prototype for ONCS, polished version for RoSEF.

Fabian has solid soldering skills, a backend Python programming background, access to a Bambu Lab FDM printer and an Elegoo resin printer, and is currently in a familiarization and mental-mapping phase — not yet ready to order or build.

A key differentiator Fabian wants over commercial products like the reMarkable: a **split-screen mode** (PDF on one half, notes on the other).

---

**Current state**

Core hardware decisions have been reached:

- **Display:** 10.3" Waveshare e-ink panel with IT8951 controller
- **Digitizer:** Wacom EMR overlay (sourced from broken tablet on eBay or as bare overlay from AliExpress) — EMR preferred over AES for Linux support and batteryless pen
- **Compute:** Raspberry Pi 4 (2GB RAM)
- **Power:** 6000mAh LiPo + PCB protection, TP4056 charger, MT3608 boost converter, USB-C breakout
- **Orientation:** Portrait
- **Storage:** 64GB Samsung or SanDisk Endurance MicroSD; USB-A port for external SSD expandability
- **Enclosure:** PETG (Bambu) for structural parts, resin (Elegoo) for front bezel and detail parts; N52 magnets for pen holder
- **Touch:** Capacitive touch not a priority, but welcome if the sourced Wacom overlay includes it

Key technical ground covered: SPI wiring (Pi 4 ↔ IT8951, 8 GPIO pins), I2C for capacitive touch, USB/I2C for Wacom EMR, EMR/capacitive layer coexistence, palm rejection via pen hover detection + ~500ms re-enable delay, LiPo safety, and the physical display layer stack.

A full parts list (~15 items), cost estimate (~$245–285), 2-month sprint plan, and resource list have already been compiled.

---

**On the horizon**

- RoSEF version: potential upgrade to proper USB-C multifunction port and overall polish
- Software development (not yet started; Fabian indicated it was too early to plan this in detail)
- Ordering and physical build (pending readiness)

---

**Tools & resources**

Already identified and provided to Fabian:

- **GitHub:** Waveshare IT8951 driver, PaperTTY, awesome-reMarkable, GregDMeyer Python IT8951, PineNote Debian image, scanlime Wacom EMR schematics
- **Communities:** reMarkable unofficial Discord, PINE64 Discord, relevant Reddit communities
- **Reference:** Waveshare IT8951 documentation, related project pages

---

**Approach & patterns**

- Prefers **concise, direct answers** — pushes back when responses go too deep too early or front-load detail before it's needed
- Thinks in phases; doesn't want to plan steps that aren't yet relevant
- Casual communication style; responds well to practical, grounded guidance
